account: At about 05:30 on 5 February 2026 the AI門神 (AI door god) system flagged smoke in a first-floor office and machine room, empty after hours. The system is run by 立達軟體 (LEADERG Inc.) over the closed-circuit television of Beigang Wude Temple, Yunlin County, Taiwan. It messaged the front desk, the general manager and chairman 林安樂, in Japan, by LINE. The night-duty clerk reached the room with an extinguisher within a minute. At 05:33 overheated lithium batteries beside a tool charger burst and flames spread. UDN reports that a residential smoke alarm (住警器) sounded as well. Staff called the emergency number 119 at 05:36. Yunlin County Fire Bureau crews arrived at 05:44, controlled the fire at 06:10 and put it out at 06:14. Ten square meters burned. Nobody was hurt. The main hall and statues were untouched. The Third Brigade commander 陳岳謄 attributed the containment to the building's reinforced-concrete structure and the crews' quick arrival without mentioning the AI. On 25 August 2026, after the Zhinan Temple fire in Taipei, UDN reported that Wude Temple still relied on its AI alarm system combined with the cameras.

ai_role.statement: The system's documented contribution is the first alert. TVBS reports that the system detected smoke at 05:30. UDN reports that the lithium batteries burst at about 05:33, while repeating the chairman's claim of a one-minute lead. The precise warning interval remains unresolved. It messaged the front desk, the general manager and the chairman in sequence over LINE. That is how a chairman asleep in Nara came to follow the fire on the temple's cameras. The suppression was human. The clerk's extinguisher failed once the batteries burst. The Yunlin County Fire Bureau's eight trucks and eighteen firefighters, called at 05:36, controlled the fire at 06:10. UDN reports that a residential smoke alarm (住警器) sounded as well. The Third Brigade commander 陳岳謄 attributed the containment to the building's reinforced-concrete structure and the crews' quick arrival without mentioning the AI. The LINE relay from the vendor is the chairman's account, not the bureau's.

fields.account: At about 05:30 on 5 February 2026 the AI門神 (AI door god) system flagged smoke in a first-floor office and machine room, empty after hours. The system is run by 立達軟體 (LEADERG Inc.) over the closed-circuit television of Beigang Wude Temple, Yunlin County, Taiwan. It messaged the front desk, the general manager and chairman 林安樂, in Japan, by LINE. The night-duty clerk reached the room with an extinguisher within a minute. At 05:33 overheated lithium batteries beside a tool charger burst and flames spread. UDN reports that a residential smoke alarm (住警器) sounded as well. Staff called the emergency number 119 at 05:36. Yunlin County Fire Bureau crews arrived at 05:44, controlled the fire at 06:10 and put it out at 06:14. Ten square meters burned. Nobody was hurt. The main hall and statues were untouched. The Third Brigade commander 陳岳謄 attributed the containment to the building's reinforced-concrete structure and the crews' quick arrival without mentioning the AI. On 25 August 2026, after the Zhinan Temple fire in Taipei, UDN reported that Wude Temple still relied on its AI alarm system combined with the cameras.

The recorded follow-up says: In August 2026, after the Zhinan Temple fire in Taipei, UDN reported Wude Temple still relying on its AI alarm system combined with the cameras, recounting the February fire as the case that proved it; no other temple adopting the system is reported.

ratings.reason: The temple's loss was the contents of one first-floor office of about ten square meters (staff lockers, some tea, sweets, incense and joss paper). The main hall, statues and worship areas were untouched. The temple stayed open in the run-up to the Lunar New Year crowds. The fire bureau credited the reinforced-concrete structure and its own eight-minute arrival for the containment. A conventional smoke alarm sounded as well. The share attributable to the AI alert is an earlier warning, whose length the sources do not settle.

display.answer: The fire was reportedly extinguished without injuries or damage to the main hall. The share of containment attributable to AI is uncertain.

fields.purpose: AI門神 (“AI door god: temple AI fire-and-theft prevention system”) was built to run AI image recognition over a temple's existing closed-circuit television. It was built to detect excess smoke, flame and suspicious behavior. It alerts staff by text message, LINE or email. CTS reported in December 2024 that Wude Temple's door-god system would sound an alarm at once on abnormal smoke. Flagging smoke before a fire was its designed purpose.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Filed as a protective response with prevention unproven, because the counterfactual is not shown. The temple's timeline, as reported by TVBS, UDN, NOWnews, 觀傳媒 and CTS, documents the smoke alert at 05:30 and its relay over LINE to the front desk, the general manager and the chairman. The Yunlin County Fire Bureau's figures document the outcome. UDN reports that a residential smoke alarm (住警器) sounded as well, and a clerk was on night duty. The Third Brigade commander 陳岳謄 credited the reinforced-concrete structure and the crews' quick arrival without mentioning the AI. The Monitor's date of 4 February is the date in Coordinated Universal Time. Every source puts the fire at about 05:30 on 5 February 2026 Taiwan time (21:30 on 4 February in Coordinated Universal Time), so the date observed is 5 February. The temple's log gives 05:51 for control of the fire, and the fire bureau gives 06:10 for control and 06:14 for extinction; the record uses the bureau's times. The cause, a tool charger and lithium batteries, is the chairman's account. UDN's first report says that the bureau was still investigating, and the secretary general 蘇建華 told TVBS that he suspected wiring. The chairman names the vendor as 立達軟體. Its identity as LEADERG Inc. and the system's design come from Advantech's case study of April 2025, which is partner-authored and cited only as an additional source. The four yam.com links in the Monitor are syndications of 觀傳媒 (two), 台灣好報 and 創新聞. UDN, NOWnews and NextApple quote the chairman's Facebook post. 觀傳媒, 台灣好報 and 創新聞 quote the fire bureau's statements, and CTS quotes the Beigang sub-station chief 陳思淵. The Monitor's country field is “Chinese Taipei”, and the record says Taiwan, as every source does.

fields.account: At about 05:30 on 5 February 2026 the AI門神 (AI door god) system flagged smoke in a first-floor office and machine room, empty after hours. The system is run by 立達軟體 (LEADERG Inc.) over the closed-circuit television of Beigang Wude Temple, Yunlin County, Taiwan. It messaged the front desk, the general manager and chairman 林安樂, in Japan, by LINE. The night-duty clerk reached the room with an extinguisher within a minute. At 05:33 overheated lithium batteries beside a tool charger burst and flames spread. UDN reports that a residential smoke alarm (住警器) sounded as well. Staff called the emergency number 119 at 05:36. Yunlin County Fire Bureau crews arrived at 05:44, controlled the fire at 06:10 and put it out at 06:14. Ten square meters burned. Nobody was hurt. The main hall and statues were untouched. The Third Brigade commander 陳岳謄 attributed the containment to the building's reinforced-concrete structure and the crews' quick arrival without mentioning the AI. On 25 August 2026, after the Zhinan Temple fire in Taipei, UDN reported that Wude Temple still relied on its AI alarm system combined with the cameras.
fields.summary: The AI door god camera system from LEADERG flagged smoke in an empty office at Beigang Wude Temple before a battery fire, and the fire burned ten square meters with nobody hurt.

echoes.setting: OECD AIM 2023-09-12-f6ac: ALERTCalifornia's AI flags a 3 am smoke column near Mount Laguna, human operators verify it and Cal Fire holds the fire (camera smoke detection with a human in the loop and a brigade response).
OECD AIM 2025-09-13-b5dc: Taichung EPB's AI smoke-recognition system catches a serial roadside waste burner (Taiwanese camera smoke analytics in a different use).

must_hold: The alert reaches a person who can act within minutes. At an unstaffed site the lead time is worth little.
The camera covers the rooms where fires start (here an office and machine room with chargers, beside stored joss paper), not only the shrine.
The AI alert complements conventional detectors rather than replacing them. A residential smoke alarm sounded here as well.
produced_by: A camera-analytics system (AI門神) already watching the office over the temple's existing CCTV. It was set to alert on small amounts of smoke and to message a named chain of people (front desk, general manager, chairman) over LINE.
A staffed night watch. The temple has kept someone on duty every night since it moved to the site in 1980 (民國69年). So the alert had a clerk a minute away with an extinguisher.
Smoke appeared before the lithium batteries burst, allowing an alert before the fire intensified. The precise warning interval remains unresolved.
A fire brigade eight minutes away and a reinforced-concrete annex that held the fire to one room, as the Third Brigade commander said.

purpose: AI門神 (“AI door god: temple AI fire-and-theft prevention system”) was built to run AI image recognition over a temple's existing closed-circuit television. It was built to detect excess smoke, flame and suspicious behavior. It alerts staff by text message, LINE or email. CTS reported in December 2024 that Wude Temple's door-god system would sound an alarm at once on abnormal smoke. Flagging smoke before a fire was its designed purpose.

ratings.reason: The temple's loss was the contents of one first-floor office of about ten square meters (staff lockers, some tea, sweets, incense and joss paper). The main hall, statues and worship areas were untouched. The temple stayed open in the run-up to the Lunar New Year crowds. The fire bureau credited the reinforced-concrete structure and its own eight-minute arrival for the containment. A conventional smoke alarm sounded as well. The share attributable to the AI alert is an earlier warning, whose length the sources do not settle.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Filed as a protective response with prevention unproven, because the counterfactual is not shown. The temple's timeline, as reported by TVBS, UDN, NOWnews, 觀傳媒 and CTS, documents the smoke alert at 05:30 and its relay over LINE to the front desk, the general manager and the chairman. The Yunlin County Fire Bureau's figures document the outcome. UDN reports that a residential smoke alarm (住警器) sounded as well, and a clerk was on night duty. The Third Brigade commander 陳岳謄 credited the reinforced-concrete structure and the crews' quick arrival without mentioning the AI. The Monitor's date of 4 February is the date in Coordinated Universal Time. Every source puts the fire at about 05:30 on 5 February 2026 Taiwan time (21:30 on 4 February in Coordinated Universal Time), so the date observed is 5 February. The temple's log gives 05:51 for control of the fire, and the fire bureau gives 06:10 for control and 06:14 for extinction; the record uses the bureau's times. The cause, a tool charger and lithium batteries, is the chairman's account. UDN's first report says that the bureau was still investigating, and the secretary general 蘇建華 told TVBS that he suspected wiring. The chairman names the vendor as 立達軟體. Its identity as LEADERG Inc. and the system's design come from Advantech's case study of April 2025, which is partner-authored and cited only as an additional source. The four yam.com links in the Monitor are syndications of 觀傳媒 (two), 台灣好報 and 創新聞. UDN, NOWnews and NextApple quote the chairman's Facebook post. 觀傳媒, 台灣好報 and 創新聞 quote the fire bureau's statements, and CTS quotes the Beigang sub-station chief 陳思淵. The Monitor's country field is “Chinese Taipei”, and the record says Taiwan, as every source does.
